title: Two stops too far
setting: Saturday morning. Yuki and Mai have arranged to meet at a station at ten and go shopping. Mai came by bus through heavy traffic and is already there. She calls Yuki, who picks up on the platform of a different station further down the line.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, yuki? watashi, mou eki tsuita yo. ima doko?
lines.ja: もしもし、ユキ？私、もう駅着いたよ。今どこ？
lines.kana: もしもし、ゆき？わたし、もうえきついたよ。いまどこ？
lines.english: Hello, Yuki? I'm at the station already. Where are you?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mai, gomen! sore ga ne, ima chigau eki ni iru no.
lines.ja: マイ、ごめん！それがね、今違う駅にいるの。
lines.kana: まい、ごめん！それがね、いまちがうえきにいるの。
lines.english: Mai, I'm so sorry! The thing is, I'm at the wrong station.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.english: What? The wrong station? How come?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: densha, saisho wa kekkou kondeta n da kedo, me no mae no seki ga aite ne.
lines.ja: 電車、最初はけっこう混んでたんだけど、目の前の席が空いてね。
lines.kana: でんしゃ、さいしょはけっこうこんでたんだけど、めのまえのせきがあいてね。
lines.english: The train was pretty packed at first, but then the seat right in front of me came free.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: aa, seki aitara suwatchau yo ne. de, nechatta?
lines.ja: ああ、席空いたら座っちゃうよね。で、寝ちゃった？
lines.kana: ああ、せきあいたらすわっちゃうよね。で、ねちゃった？
lines.english: Oh, when a seat comes free you just have to sit, right? And then you fell asleep?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou na no. kimochi yokute, futaeki mo norisugoshichatta.
lines.ja: そうなの。気持ちよくて、二駅も乗り過ごしちゃった。
lines.kana: そうなの。きもちよくて、ふたえきものりすごしちゃった。
lines.english: Yep. It was so comfy that I went two whole stops past mine.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: futaeki mo? demo wakaru. watashi mo kono aida, oriru eki o norisugoshichatta.
lines.ja: 二駅も？でもわかる。私もこの間、降りる駅を乗り過ごしちゃった。
lines.kana: ふたえきも？でもわかる。わたしもこのあいだ、おりるえきをのりすごしちゃった。
lines.english: Two stops? I get it, though. I went past my stop the other day too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mai wa? basu, daijoubu datta? doyoubi wa michi komu desho?
lines.ja: マイは？バス、大丈夫だった？土曜日は道混むでしょ？
lines.kana: まいは？ばす、だいじょうぶだった？どようびはみちこむでしょ？
lines.english: What about you? Was the bus OK? The roads always get busy on Saturdays, don't they?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, michi sugoku kondeta. demo hayaku uchi deta kara, maniatta.
lines.ja: うん、道すごく混んでた。でも早くうち出たから、間に合った。
lines.kana: うん、みちすごくこんでた。でもはやくうちでたから、まにあった。
lines.english: Yeah, the traffic was really heavy. But I left home early, so I made it on time.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yokatta. watashi wa densha na noni okurechatte, honto gomen.
lines.ja: よかった。私は電車なのに遅れちゃって、ほんとごめん。
lines.kana: よかった。わたしはでんしゃなのにおくれちゃって、ほんとごめん。
lines.english: Oh, good. And here I am on the train and still late. I'm so sorry.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ii yo, ii yo. de, kotchi no eki ni wa nanji ni tsuku?
lines.ja: いいよ、いいよ。で、こっちの駅には何時に着く？
lines.kana: いいよ、いいよ。で、こっちのえきにはなんじにつく？
lines.english: It's fine, really. So what time will you get to the station here?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tsugi no densha de modoru kara, juuji han ni wa tsuku to omou.
lines.ja: 次の電車で戻るから、十時半には着くと思う。
lines.kana: つぎのでんしゃでもどるから、じゅうじはんにはつくとおもう。
lines.english: I'll come back on the next train, so I should be there by half past ten.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. jaa, eki no mae de matteru ne.
lines.ja: うん。じゃあ、駅の前で待ってるね。
lines.kana: うん。じゃあ、えきのまえでまってるね。
lines.english: OK. I'll wait for you out front, then.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, densha kita. suitete, seki mo ippai aiteru yo.
lines.ja: あ、電車来た。空いてて、席もいっぱい空いてるよ。
lines.kana: あ、でんしゃきた。すいてて、せきもいっぱいあいてるよ。
lines.english: Oh, here's the train. It's nearly empty, there are loads of free seats.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: dame dame, suwatcha! mata norisugoshichau yo.
lines.ja: だめだめ、座っちゃ！また乗り過ごしちゃうよ。
lines.kana: だめだめ、すわっちゃ！またのりすごしちゃうよ。
lines.english: No, no, don't sit down! You'll go past your stop again.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: wakatta, suwaranai. eki tsuitara, sugu renraku suru ne.
lines.ja: わかった、座らない。駅着いたら、すぐ連絡するね。
lines.kana: わかった、すわらない。えきついたら、すぐれんらくするね。
lines.english: OK, I won't sit. I'll let you know as soon as I get to the station.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kaeri wa nete mo ii yo. okoshite ageru kara.
lines.ja: 帰りは寝てもいいよ。起こしてあげるから。
lines.kana: かえりはねてもいいよ。おこしてあげるから。
lines.english: On the way home you can sleep. I'll wake you up.

choices.english: Mai's bus got stuck in traffic, so Yuki is waiting for her at the station.
Yuki missed her train, so she'll take the next one and Mai will meet her at another station.
Yuki fell asleep on the train and went past her stop, so Mai, who came by bus, is the one waiting.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Mai is already at the station (mou eki tsuita yo). Lines 2-6: Yuki is at the wrong station because a seat came free, she sat down, fell asleep and went two stops past hers (futaeki mo norisugoshichatta). A swaps them: the roads were jammed (line 9), but Mai left home early and made it on time, and it's Yuki who is late (line 10). B: Yuki didn't miss a train. She rode past her stop, and she's coming back on the next train (line 12) while Mai waits outside their station (line 13).

questions.english: You're meeting Tanaka-san at the station for a work trip. He calls you: "Hello, it's Tanaka. Where are you now?" You've just got to the station. Tell him.
questions.ja: もしもし、田中です。今どこですか？
questions.kana: もしもし、たなかです。いまどこですか？
questions.romaji: moshimoshi, tanaka desu. ima doko desu ka?
questions.answer: Say you've arrived, using the past of tsuku in the polite form: ima eki ni tsukimashita.

modelAnswers.english: I've just got to the station.

modelAnswers.romaji: sakki eki ni tsukimashita. ima, eki no mae ni imasu.
modelAnswers.ja: さっき駅に着きました。今、駅の前にいます。
modelAnswers.english: I got to the station a moment ago. I'm out front now.

questions.explanation: 'I'm here' is the past of tsuku: Mai opens with mou eki tsuita yo (line 1), and Yuki promises eki tsuitara, sugu renraku suru ne (line 16). To your manager, use the -masu form, tsukimashita. eki ni touchaku shimashita is correct but stiff, the language of announcements and work emails. In conversation you arrive with tsuku. Friends drop ni (eki tsuita), but keep it with Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Yuki asks how Mai's bus ride went. What does Mai say about the roads?
questions.ja: マイさんは、道について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、みちについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, michi ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?
questions.explanation: Line 9: un, michi sugoku kondeta, which answers Yuki's doyoubi wa michi komu desho? (line 8). A road full of cars is konderu, the same verb as a packed train (densha ... kondeta, line 4). B, isogashikatta, is English 'busy' word for word, but isogashii is for people and their time, never a road. C, suiteta, is the opposite: clear roads. Mai only made it on time because she left home early (hayaku uchi deta kara, maniatta).

questions.english: Yuki's train back pulls in. What does she tell Mai about it?
questions.ja: 次の電車が来て、ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: つぎのでんしゃがきて、ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: tsugi no densha ga kite, yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: It's packed, but the seat right in front of her has just come free.
It's nearly empty, with lots of free seats.
It's packed, so she'll have to stand all the way.

questions.explanation: Line 14: suitete, seki mo ippai aiteru yo. aiteru is about seats: a seat that has come free (seki ga aku). suiteru is about the whole train: it isn't crowded. Together they mean an empty train with plenty of free seats, which is why Mai cries dame dame, suwatcha! (line 15). A mixes this up with line 4, the crowded train on the way there, where one seat (me no mae no seki) came free. C would be konderu, which is how the first train was, not this one.

questions.english: You're meeting Kenta, but you fell asleep on the train and went one stop past your station. When you call him, he says: "What happened? You're late." Tell him what happened.
questions.answer: Apologise and say you rode past your stop, with norisugoshita or norisugoshichatta: gomen, nechatte, hitoeki norisugoshichatta.

modelAnswers.ja: ごめん！寝ちゃって、一駅乗り過ごしちゃった。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry! I fell asleep and went one stop too far.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen ne. oriru eki o norisugoshichatte, ima modotteru tokoro.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめんね。降りる駅を乗り過ごしちゃって、今戻ってるところ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry. I went past my stop, and I'm on my way back now.

questions.explanation: Riding past your stop is norisugosu (noru 'ride' + sugosu 'let go by'), nearly always in the past. Yuki's futaeki mo norisugoshichatta (line 6) counts how far she went in stops, and Mai's oriru eki o norisugoshichatta (line 7) names the stop with o, not the ni of eki ni tsuku. Not eki o nogashita: nogasu is for a train that left without you. misu shita doesn't work for a stop either.

newWords.english: right in front of you (me = eyes)
two stops, two stations (hitoeki = one stop)
(a train, road or shop) is empty, not crowded; the opposite of konderu
